title: Where two or three (Matthew 18:15–20)
hook: go to the one who wronged you, alone; and where two or three gather, he's there
tomorrow: so how many times do you have to forgive the same thing?

segments.voice: Yesterday, their angels: a child in the middle, and the little ones nearest to God's face. Their angels see God. Today, the hard conversation.

Screenshot it. Post it. Tell the whole group chat. That's one way to handle being wronged, and it's fast. Matthew eighteen starts somewhere much quieter, and it answers yesterday's question directly: "If thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother." Start private. And notice the goal. Not winning. Gaining your brother back.
screen: `SCREENSHOT IT. POST IT.` → `BETWEEN THEE AND HIM ALONE.` → `THE GOAL: GAIN HIM BACK.`

segments.voice: Only if that fails does the circle widen: take one or two others along, so that "in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established." Then the church. And if he won't hear even the church, let him be to you as a heathen man and a publican. That sounds like a door slamming, but some readers notice how Matthew's Jesus treats publicans, tax collectors: he eats with them. Then comes the line some people stitch on pillows: "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them." Here's the thing worth telling a friend: in Matthew, it doesn't come after a worship service. It comes right after the steps of a hard conversation. Two or three is the size of the room where someone says, you hurt me, and someone listens. That small, uncomfortable room is the one he promises to be in.
screen: `ONE OR TWO WITNESSES.` · `AS A HEATHEN AND A PUBLICAN?` · `TWO OR THREE GATHERED.` · `THE ROOM OF THE HARD TALK.` · then, large: `THERE AM I.`

segments.voice: Two voices sound different from one: they have to wait for each other. If someone is with you, sit side by side, close enough to hear each other breathe, and say one short line out loud together, slowly, twice; if you pray, it can be today's line, where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them. If you're alone, say it once, out loud, and listen to your own voice in the room. Then, in the quiet, let one face come to mind: the person you'd want sitting next to you for it.
Where two or three. The small gathering, even the hard conversation, where Jesus promises, there am I in the midst of them.
Keep this: there am I, even in a room of two, even when it’s awkward. See you tomorrow.

chat.says: Kayla from altos posted a "choking" gif in the choir chat after my solo. reply to everyone or no?
options: Not in the group. Matthew 18 starts private: talk to Kayla alone first, to win her back.
Reply to all so it's on record. Two or three witnesses, like Jesus said.
Leave the chat. If she won't listen, treat her as a heathen, like Matthew says.
chat.meaning: Matthew 18:15: go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone. Witnesses and the wider circle come only if that fails.

trespass.meaning: older English for wrong or sin against someone

publican.meaning: a tax collector, in the King James

heathen.meaning: older English for an outsider to the faith
